claim: Replacing the constant start (R=2/3) with a discretized Gaussian exp(-0.5((i-c)/sigma)^2) on N=2001 and optimizing sigma raises R to 0.7210, consistent with the analytic Gaussian value 1/sqrt(2)≈0.7071 (slightly above it due to discretization).

Random-restart hill climbing with block perturbations and progressive upsampling to fine resolution (N=3200) reaches R=0.8116, the best of generation 1, far above the Gaussian baseline 0.7210; the resulting f*f is much flatter-topped (16% of knots within 0.1% of max vs 1.1% for the Gaussian) with its peak shifted off-center to 0.29 of support.

Multiscale random multiplicative coordinate ascent from the constant start reaches R=0.7955 at N=400, second-best in generation 1, again producing a broad f*f top (2.75%/9.86%/28.71% of knots within 0.1%/1%/5% of max) with peak at 0.416 of support.

Parametric family search over generalized Gaussians exp(-|x|^p) and compact bumps (1-x^2)_+^a with golden-section refinement reaches only R=0.7238, barely above the pure Gaussian 0.7210; smooth symmetric parametric families are near-optimal within their class but cannot match the non-parametric hill-climbed shapes (0.81).

Naive single-coordinate multiplicative hill climbing from a random exponential start (N=1000, sigma=0.2, restarts every 5000 non-improving steps) stalls at R=0.6567, below even the constant 2/3; single-coordinate moves on a high-dimensional shape are too weak to escape the random start.

Higher R correlates with a flatter, broader f*f top and an off-center peak: the best constructions (p0003 R=0.812, p0004 R=0.796) have 16% and 2.75% of knots within 0.1% of max with peaks at 0.29 and 0.42 of support, versus 1.1% and peak at 0.50 for the Gaussian (p0005 R=0.721); flattening the autoconvolution maximum relative to its L2 mass is the operative lever.

Exact analytic-gradient projected ascent with backtracking, applied to p0003's h (N=3200) and upsampled to N=25600, does not move the score: 0.811594 -> 0.811595 (+0.000001) in 28.8 s CPU, with the f*f plateau fraction unchanged at 16.03% within 0.1% of max and peak still at 0.290 of support. The same gradient code from p0004's h (N=400 -> 12800) gives 0.795501 -> 0.795509 (+0.000009). So p0003 an

This confirms the Gaussian is a usable seed for coordinate ascent but lands well below p0003/p0008, and its f*f is much peakier (0.46% within

Is p0003 (R=0.8116, peak at 0.290, 16% plateau) actually the global optimum at N=3200, or just the best basin reachable from smooth starts? p0012's diverse starts all reproduced it, but they were all smooth (Fourier/Gaussian/piecewise) and at N=400. Worth testing: non-smooth or multi-bump starts at N>=1600, and whether p0008's 0.8034 basin (peak at 0.520) can be pushed past 0.8116 by the same resa

The 0.8116 barrier is a basin artifact, not a global bound: smooth-start local methods (gradient and coordinate) all converge to the same few basins (peaks at 0.29 and 0.52), while a derivative-free global search at N=32 opens a genuinely different basin (peak 0.805) that refines to 0.8521. This confirms F12's suspicion that p0003 was only the best smooth-start basin.

Annealed smoothed-max (p-norm) gradient ascent at N=3200 (p=4..64) does not move p0011 off 0.811595: +0.000000, identical score and identical plateau fraction (16.03% within 0.1%). Smoothing the max kink gives a non-zero gradient but no usable descent direction at this optimum, so the kink is not what blocks improvement.

Exact-gradient Adam ascent with multiscale upsampling applied to p0008 (N=6400) leaves the score unchanged at 0.803448 (+0.000000), confirming again that gradient methods are a no-op on these optima while coordinate descent still gains (p0019 +0.000588 on the same start).

Adaptive block coordinate descent (blocks of width 1..N/20, step-size feedback, perturb-restarts, resampling to N=12800/25600/51200) on p0008's distinct basin (peak 0.52) raises R from 0.803448 to 0.804037 (+0.000588) but stalls well below 0.8116; the peak stays at 0.520 and the plateau fraction grows only slightly (4.02% -> 4.63% within 0.1%). The 0.52-peak basin appears to top out near 0.804.

Upsampling p0010's construction to N=8001 and running finer block refinement with keep() after every climb raises R from 0.785486 to 0.786976 (+0.001490), with the f*f peak moving to 0.484 and a much sharper top (0.41% within 0.1%). Confirms that resolution resampling plus coordinate climbing still yields small gains on the Gaussian-derived basin, but far below the global-search basin.

Mass-preserving upsampling of p0018's N=2048 construction to N=4096/8192/16384 with adaptive random-block descent and per-coordinate polish does not raise R: 0.852088 -> 0.852089 (+0.000001) in 28.3 s CPU. The plateau fraction within 0.1% of max stays at 15.27% and the peak stays at 0.636, so the new global-DE basin is saturated under local refinement at these resolutions, not merely under-optimiz

Multi-seed, larger-population differential evolution at N=24/32 (popsize 30, 3 seeds, p0018's downsampled shape as one seed individual) does not find a better coarse basin than p0018's single-seed popsize-15 DE: the result is p0018's array unchanged, R=0.852088 (+0.000000), peak still at 0.805. Passing the 0.29-peak family (p0003, R=0.8116) through the global-DE machinery — mass-downsample to N=32, differential_evolution with popsize 25 and 2 seeds, then progressive 2x mass-preserving upsampling with block coordinate descent — raises R from 0.811594 to 0.819750 (+0.008156). The peak moves from 0.290 to 0.468 and the 0.1%-plateau fraction drops from 16.03% to 8.72%, so the coarse global s

Analytic-gradient Adam ascent on log R with upsampling through N=8192, plus coordinate polish and perturb/restart loops, leaves p0018's construction unchanged at R=0.852088 (+0.000000), peak 0.805, plateau 15.23% within 0.1%. Gradient methods are again a no-op on an already-optimized optimum, this time in the new global-DE basin, confirming the pattern is not specific to the 0.29/0.52-peak basins.

Smoothed-max (p-norm) gradient annealing at low N plus cumulative-mass upsampling, exact-R polish and perturbed restarts leaves p0017's construction at R=0.811595 (+0.000000), peak 0.290, plateau 16.03% within 0.1%. Replacing the exact-max kink with a smoothed max still yields no movement, so the vanishing gradient at these optima is not solely the max-kink effect.

Upsampling p0017's construction to N=200000 immediately and polishing with the exact gradient at full resolution fails on the step cap: the run reached N=204800 and was rejected (too many steps, limit 200000), with the last printed score still 0.811595. High-resolution upsampling of an existing optimum costs steps without moving R, so it must be budgeted against the step limit, not just CPU.

Seeded differential evolution at a finer coarse grid (N=64, popsize 15, bounds [0,10], init = mass-downsampled seed + 14 perturbed copies) followed by progressive 2x mass-preserving upsampling to N=4096 with block descent and polish nudges the 0.852 basin from R=0.852089 to 0.852108 (+0.000019), with the f*f peak at 0.484 and 15.80% of knots within 0.1% of max. Applying the same N=64 coarse-DE + upsample-to-6400 recipe to p0024's distinct 0.468-peak basin (R=0.819750) yields only +0.000052 (to 0.819802), far short of the predicted 0.83-0.85. The 0.468-peak basin is also saturated under this recipe; the +0.008 that p0024 got came from the initial coarse-DE discovery, not from repeated refinement.

A structured sum-of-K=6-free-rectangular-blocks family (centers, widths, heights; 18 params; DE then block/coordinate descent, rasterized to N=2048) did not finish within budget: the run stopped at the 47 s CPU limit with nothing kept because keep_best was wired to a stale variable. No score was produced, so the block family remains untested as a construction.

Replacing coordinate descent with FFT-based analytic-gradient Adam ascent on log R (plus block moves and perturb/restart) on p0014's N=32001 construction crashed with an IndexError: a boolean mask of length 16001 was applied to an array of length 32001. The gradient machinery itself was never evaluated; the failure is a shape bug in the block-perturbation mask, not evidence about gradient methods.

Analytic-gradient ascent of R (FFT-based) plus block descent and localized perturbations, applied to p0023's N=4096 construction, leaves the score unchanged at 0.852089 (+0.000000), with plateau fraction 15.27% within 0.1% and peak at 0.485. This is a fourth independent confirmation that gradient methods are a no-op on these optima.

Mass-preserving upsampling of p0023 from N=4096 through 8192 to 16384 with block-move descent and per-coordinate fine polish leaves R unchanged at 0.852089 (+0.000000), plateau 15.26% within 0.1%. This reproduces F19's saturation result on the same basin via a different code path, strengthening the claim that the 0.852 basin is locally saturated at N<=16384.

A free-knot piecewise-constant construction (K=8 segments, 7 free breakpoints + 8 free heights, 15 params, rasterized to N=2048) optimized by differential evolution then block/coordinate descent reaches R=0.832956 from scratch — a distinct basin (peak at 0.500, 1.17% plateau within 0.1%) that beats the Gaussian baseline 0.7210 and the parametric-family ceiling 0.7238, but falls short of the unifor

Simulated-annealing basin hopping with structured block/Fourier perturbations plus block descent and coordinate polish raises the saturated 0.8198 basin (p0030) by +0.000225 to 0.820028 at N=6400, with the f*f peak moving to 0.547 and plateau 8.14% within 0.1%. This is the first gain on that basin after coarse-DE+upsample (F26) had saturated it, showing an escape mechanism can still move a flat ba

Enlarging the N=64 coarse DE (popsize 40, one third uniform-random init, one third heavily perturbed seed, 7 s cap, upsample through N=1024) does not find a better coarse basin than p0029's popsize-15 seeded DE: R stays at 0.852108 (+0.000000), plateau 15.81% within 0.1%, peak at 0.716. Broader random-diverse coarse search does not escape the 0.852 basin.

Normalized-momentum analytic-gradient ascent on log R with mass-preserving upsampling to N=8192 and block coordinate polish leaves the 0.852 basin unchanged at 0.852088 (+0.000000), plateau 15.25% within 0.1%, peak at 0.805 — another confirmation that gradient methods are a no-op on these optima.

FFT-based analytic-gradient Adam ascent on R plus upsample+Adam+polish to N=8192 leaves p0023's construction at 0.852089 (+0.000000), plateau 15.26% within 0.1%, peak at 0.715. Reproduces F29/F30's saturation of the 0.852 basin under gradient refinement.

Corrected mass-resampling plus smoothed-max annealing at N=1200 with more p values and upsampling to N=40000 with longer exact-R polish and more perturbed restarts leaves the 0.29-peak basin at 0.811595 (-0.000000), plateau 16.03% within 0.1%, peak at 0.290. The 0.29-peak basin remains saturated under smoothed-max annealing regardless of resolution and budget.

Simulated-annealing basin hopping with structured perturbations (block-multiply, low-frequency Fourier, bump, global) applied to the saturated 0.852 basin at N=2048 raises R from 0.852108 to 0.852591 (+0.000483), the first escape from that basin after greedy descent, coarse DE, and mass-upsampling all failed; the f*f peak moves to 0.507 and the 0.1% plateau fraction rises to 16.82%.

Warm-starting a richer K=16 free-knot piecewise-constant DE from p0037's quantile-segmented shape, then SA basin hopping and block descent at N=4096, raises R from 0.832956 to 0.839015 (+0.006058); the result has a much sharper top (1.78%/12.66% within 0.1%/1%) and peak at 0.381, showing the free-knot family is not saturated at K=8.

A log-piecewise-linear (exponential-spline) parametrization — K=10 knots, 8 free interior positions, u_i in [-3,3], h=exp(u), 18 params — optimized by DE then block/SA polish reaches R=0.831320 from scratch at N=1024, a distinct asymmetric basin (peak at 0.594, 4.69% plateau within 0.1%, max/mean height 3.99), competitive with the free-knot line without any warm start.

Analytic-gradient Adam ascent on log R with mass-preserving upsampling to N=2048 and alternating Adam/block restarts leaves the 0.852 basin unchanged at 0.852108 (+0.000000), plateau 15.84% within 0.1%, peak at 0.484 — another confirmation that gradient methods are a no-op on this optimum.

Analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B polishing with progressive upsampling to N=8192 and perturbation restarts leaves the 0.852 basin at 0.852109 (+0.000001), plateau 15.86% within 0.1%, peak at 0.806 — the second-order gradient method is as inert as Adam on this optimum.

FFT-based block descent plus mass-preserving upscaling across N levels and per-coordinate polish on p0004's 0.312-peak construction yields only +0.000016 (0.795501 -> 0.795517), plateau 2.75% within 0.1% — the 0.795 basin is saturated against this refiner as well.

Raising the free-knot piecewise-constant DE from K=16 to K=32 (63 params, N=1024 raster, popsize 20, warm-started from p0040's quantile segmentation) raises R from 0.839015 to 0.842636 (+0.003622) at N=4096, with the f*f peak moving to 0.108 of support and a sharper top (0.90% within 0.1%, down from p0040's 1.78%). The free-knot family is still gaining with K, so it has not saturated at K=16.

A sum-of-K=5-shifted-Gaussian-bumps family (15 params: sorted centers, amplitudes, widths; DE at N=512, then mass-upsample to N=2048 with block descent, SA hopping and restarts) reaches R=0.849339 from scratch — a new basin (peak at 0.488, 18.16% of knots within 0.1% of max, largest/mean height 4.60) that beats the 0.852 basin's plateau character and nearly matches it in score. Adding an L-BFGS-B analytic-gradient polish interleaved with SA basin-hopping at increasing N (2048..16384) on the 0.8526 basin raises R from 0.852596 to 0.852735 (+0.000139) at N=8192, peak moving to 0.803, plateau 18.86% within 0.1%. This is the largest single gain on the saturated basin since F37, and unlike pure gradient ascent (F41, +1e-6) it works when interleaved with hopping.

A structured-perturbation loop with local descent plus analytic-gradient polish, with stage timings rebalanced to fill the whole budget, raises the 0.852 basin from 0.852089 to 0.852477 (+0.000389) at N=4096, peak at 0.687, plateau 18.97% within 0.1%. This is a larger gain than the SA-hopping route (F37 +0.00048 at N=2048, F45 +5e-6) and shows that budget rebalancing toward gradient polish matters

Vectorising the exact-R gradient and adding larger upsampling stages (to N=25600) plus a perturb+gradient polish loop on p0015's 0.52-peak construction leaves R unchanged at 0.803448 (+0.000000), plateau 4.02% within 0.1%. Confirms again that gradient ascent alone cannot move these optima even with more resolution and restarts.

Running a short L-BFGS (maxiter 20) after every SA perturbation at N=2048, with Metropolis acceptance on the polished points, then upsampling to 4096/8192 with a final L-BFGS, raises the 0.8527 basin from 0.852735 to 0.853049 (+0.000314) at N=4096 — the largest single-generation gain on the 0.852 basin so far. Per-hop local minimization is what makes SA basin hopping productive on the 0.852 basin: p0057 (L-BFGS after every hop) gained +0.000314, while p0060 and p0058, which kept raw-perturbation acceptance and only polished at stage ends, gained +0.000013 and +0.000010 respectively. Accepting unpolished candidates makes the Metropolis test noisy and wastes budget on non-local-minima.

Spending the whole budget on a single deep SA-hop + L-BFGS stage at high N (16384, with 32768 if time allows) instead of the N-progression gains essentially nothing: p0058 reached 0.852745 (+0.000010) and p0060 reached 0.852748 (+0.000013) from 0.852735, both within noise. High-N-only search does not exploit fine-scale structure better than the staged schedule.

Warm-starting the K=5 Gaussian-bump family (p0048, R=0.849339) by fitting 5 Gaussians and expanding to K=10 with a warm-started DE at N=1024 crashed with ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (27,) into shape (30,) — the init_pop[0] assignment used a parameter vector of the wrong length (27 vs 3*K=30). The K-doubling branch of the Gaussian-bump line remains untested.

Replacing DE+SA with analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B polish plus random-block descent and perturb+L-BFGS restarts on the K=5 Gaussian-bump family (p0048, R=0.849339) raises R only to 0.849425 (+0.000086) at N=2048, with a very flat f*f top (20.84% of knots within 0.1% of max, peak at 0.285). Gradient polish on the bump family is nearly a no-op, consistent with the saturation pattern of F11/F41.

Adding a Gauss-Newton active-set polish (dense A.T @ A over near-max knots) at N=32768 crashes with MemoryError: cannot allocate 2.00 GiB for a (16384, 16384) float64 array. Dense normal-equation matrices at high N are infeasible; any active-set polish must use sparse or matrix-free solves.

Adding a post-downsample polish, longer SA cooling, an extra 16384 refinement stage, a 5th perturbation kind (global multiplicative noise) and time-seeded RNG to p0057's per-hop-polished SA raises R from 0.853049 to 0.853076 (+0.000028) at N=8192, plateau 8.47% within 0.1%, peak at 0.561. Starting the per-hop-polished SA ladder coarser still (N=512 for the first 35% of budget, then N=1024 to 65%, N=2048 to 85%, final N=4096 L-BFGS) raises the 0.8533 basin from 0.853263 to 0.853368 (+0.000105) at N=512, with the f*f peak at 0.821 and plateau 11.90% within 0.1%. The gain is smaller than p0065's N=1024-first ladder (+0.000214), so N=512 is not clearly better than N=1024 as the startin

Deepening the per-hop L-BFGS polish (maxiter 300, 0.25 s cap instead of 25/0.03 s) in a single N=1024 SA hop loop until 75% of budget leaves the 0.853263 basin unchanged (+0.000000). So the short per-hop polish is not the binding constraint: the hops are already reaching essentially the same local minima, and spending the budget on fewer, better-converged hops buys nothing.

A short L-BFGS-B analytic-gradient polish after every SA hop, with smoothing/edge perturbations and a final long polish to fill the budget, raises the 0.852735 basin to 0.853201 (+0.000466) at N=8192, peak at 0.507, plateau 12.79% within 0.1%. This is the largest single-generation gain on the 0.852 basin and confirms per-hop gradient polish as the productive mechanism.

Adding a 32768 upsample stage and a repeated final L-BFGS polish loop (re-invoked until no improvement) to the 0.853076 construction raises R to 0.853290 (+0.000214) at N=8192, peak at 0.746, plateau 5.71% within 0.1%. Fine-scale polish still yields small gains on this basin, unlike the pure-upsample attempts that saturated.

Warm-starting a K=10 Gaussian-bump DE (3K params, popsize 20, seeded from a least-squares K=5 fit split into 10 bumps) plus hop-SA on the K=5 family raises R from 0.849425 to 0.849448 (+0.000023) at N=1024, peak at 0.152, plateau 20.89% within 0.1%. Doubling K gives almost nothing, so the Gaussian-bump family is capacity-saturated near 0.8494 and cannot close the gap to 0.8533.

Replacing coordinate descent with FFT-based analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B, multiscale upsampling to N=12800 and structured perturbation restarts raises the 0.52-peak basin from 0.803448 to 0.803703 (+0.000255) at N=12800, peak at 0.316, plateau 4.26% within 0.1%. This is the first gradient method to move this basin, contradicting the earlier no-op results on it.

Shifting the SA hop ladder to finer N levels (1024->2048->4096->8192) with re-anchoring to the global best after each improvement, a smoother 6-kind perturbation mix (block widths down to N/128, Fourier k up to 8, Gaussian bumps) and a longer final L-BFGS raises the 0.8534 basin from 0.853368 to 0.855086 (+0.001718) at N=512, the largest single-generation gain in many generations; the f*f top flat

Pushing the hop ladder one step coarser (N=256 for 15% of budget, then 512, then 1024) plus a 2048->16384 L-BFGS upsample ladder yields only +0.000023 (0.853368 -> 0.853391) at N=8192, far below the +5e-5 to +2e-4 predicted; the N=256 stage does not pay, so the productive scale floor is around N=512-1024, not lower.
